newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 25.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The FCC Chairman Clinton plans to nominate is William Kennard.
* Microsoft improperly barred certain employees from lucrative benefit plans by wrongly classifying them as temporary or contract workers.
* The US and the E.U. are embroiled in a growing number of trade disputes.
* Mallinckrodt 's planned purchase of Nellcor Puritan makes strategic sense, industry experts say, but it also saddles the hospital-products firm with a significant financial burden.
* The FASB said companies must continue to adjust their net income any time there is a change in federal taxes that could have an effect on the companies' corporate investments.
* General Motors is expected to have closed six assembly plants by this morning as a result of parts shortages from a strike at a transmission plant.
* The NASD will soon propose a system that could speed the association's detection of trading abuses by dealers on the Nasdaq market.
* America Online reversed its stance and said it won't hand over its customers' home phone numbers to telemarketers.
* Delta Air Lines directors named an acting nonexecutive chairman and actinig CEO.
* Digital Equipment reported fiscal fourth-quarter net that slightly exceeded expectations, reflecting cost-cutting measures.
* Asian currencies continued their plunge.
* Russia unveiled moves intended to stabilize the county's industrial decline.
* Tokyo shares closed mixed, with Nikkei 225 rising 155.72 points to 20286.23, the benchmark average's first first gain in four sessions.
* Stock prices rose, with major indexes posting records.
* Gateway 2000 is scrambling to win large-business customers for its personal computers.
* Pork-belly futures rose to a limit-up close on rumors of new Japanese demand.
* Silicone breast implant testimony given by plaintiff's scientific experts apparently fell short of providing compelling evidence linking the silicone implants to immune-system illnesses.
* A unit of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, one of Hong Kong's three largest conglomerates, found strong global demand for $2 billion of debt yesterday, despite concerns about Hong Kong's political future.

* Among the top performers in Latin America's first half telephone stock rally, American depository shares of the dominant telephone companies in Argentina, Chile, Mexico, Peru, Venezuela, and Brazil were hammered in mid-July amid a round of currency jitters.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
